problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Using Row Operations

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 4 & 13\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".
